prompt: Please generate an image. Locked painterly style: hand-painted stylized game art, chunky readable shapes, detail painted not modelled, mid-level detail, softer muted colours with gentle saturation, epic and luminous, never grim. The palette's warm gold and cool teal are painted into the surfaces, but the light is flat, even studio light: no strong key light, no cast shadows, no rim light. Use the attached images only as reference as described: the first attachment is always the style reference for palette and brushwork; later attachments are the approved designs to keep. Game-asset reference sheet for 3D modelling, wide landscape 16:9. Plain light neutral grey background, no scene, no sky, no clouds, no floating rock, no ground plane, a soft contact shadow only. Every piece fully isolated with clear space around it, nothing overlapping, nothing touching the edge, arranged in tidy rows, each with a small neat hand-lettered label underneath. MODULAR KIT PIECES sheet: Redraw of the attached reference sheet to the current spec: keep exactly the same pieces, their order, names and sizes. Old-world ruin style on a 4 m module and 6 m storey, 1 m thick razor-clean pale stone (#F3ECD9) with one standard 0.5 m inset channel, dead (dark groove) or lit (soft teal glow), a ring motif, a little moss; monumental and exact, not Greek or Roman, not sci-fi. Row 1 channel inlays, flat 4 x 4 m insert tiles with the 0.5 m channel, each shown dead and lit side by side plus a small three-quarter view: "Channel Inlay - Straight", "Channel Inlay - Corner (90°)", "Channel Inlay - T-Junction", "Channel Inlay - Cross", "Channel Inlay - Circle Node", each labelled "4 x 4 m (channel 0.5 m)". Row 2 glyph plates, 4 x 4 m and 0.2 m thick, with simple precise geometric glyphs (circles, arcs, lines, no letters), each intact and broken: "Glyph Plate A - Concentric Circle", "Glyph Plate B - Arc Node", "Glyph Plate C - Line Node". Row 3 floating pale stone shards hovering above a faint teal glow: "Floating Fragments (Small) ~0.5 m each", "Floating Fragments (Medium) ~1 m each", "Floating Fragments (Large) ~2 m each" (mossy tops). Row 4 overgrowth attachments, each alone with a dotted outline of the block edge it attaches to: "Root Cluster (Edge) 4 x 1 m (drape up to 2 m)", "Moss Drape 4 x 1 m (drape up to 3 m)", "Moss Cap (Top) 4 x 4 m (0.3 m thick)", "Sapling (Crack) ~1 x 1 m (up to 2 m tall)". No other pieces. Show each piece as an orthographic front elevation (no perspective) with a small three-quarter view beside it, on faint module grid lines, with its name and size (for example "3 x 4 m") in the label. Thick, solid forms, no thin parts. A plain neutral 1.8 m human silhouette labelled "1.8 m" stands on the sheet for scale, with everything at true scale to it. Title at the top: "Old world kit: details".
